key_insight: Muon can be interpreted as an implicit residual connection: orthogonalizing updates may reduce immediate gradient matching but preserve representations for later layers.
engineering_relevance: This perspective suggests optimizer design should balance fast local descent with keeping intermediate features broadly usable for downstream computation.
method: Study Muon through a mechanistic lens rather than only as a performance heuristic.
Analyze controlled linear optimization settings to isolate the trade-off between fitting the local target and preserving representations.
Compare update directions and their downstream usefulness under orthogonalized versus standard optimization behavior.
evidence_signal: The paper uses controlled linear optimization experiments to show that Muon can learn representations that fit more slowly locally but are easier for downstream layers to exploit.
watch_item: Orthogonalization may hurt short-term gradient fidelity, so benefits could depend on task structure and may not transfer uniformly to all training regimes.
